posts.name: Ross Haber
posts.text:
The Nasdaq has pulled back sharply to its 200-day EMA over the past few sessions and managed only a modest bounce this afternoon, marking Day 1 of its current rally count.

The S&P 500 has fallen well below its declining 50-day SMA but continues to trade well above its rising 200-day SMA, demonstrating greater relative strength than the Nasdaq. Today’s modest advance also marks Day 1 of a new rally count for the S&P 500.

The Russell 2000 is struggling to hold above its 200-day SMA, while the Dow has weakened considerably over the past few sessions.

Overall, the major indexes remain in poor shape, and market breadth continues to deteriorate. Today’s session produced just 133 new highs versus 360 new lows.

Earnings season has done little to spark a meaningful recovery so far. The upcoming midterm elections could also influence market sentiment and price action in the days ahead.

Among leading growth stocks, the most promising setups are currently concentrated in medical/healthcare and retail. Very few technology names are appearing on my screens, and even oil and gas stocks have weakened over the past couple of sessions.

I remain 100% in cash until the market shows a sustainable uptrend taking shape. The new Day 1 rally counts are merely the starting point of potential recovery attempts; they don't confirm a new uptrend. The soonest a confirmation day can appear is on day 4 of the rally count.

For now, capital preservation takes priority. I’ll remain patient, monitor the market’s response, and wait for stronger evidence before committing capital.
